Notice how components are mounted on top of the cards. This is done so that you can see the actual circuit you are working on.
These components are mounted in holes drilled through the experiment card. They are secured to the card by solder.

SOLDER - Solder is the silver metal material used to make electrical connections. It is a tin and lead alloy that melts when heated. A soldering iron is used to melt solder around the component and circuit card. When the iron is removed, the solder hardens making a permanent connection.
Solder lands on the back of the card connect circuit components together.
SOLDER LANDS - Solder lands are thin strips bonded to the experiment card. Solder lands connect one component to another to form circuits.
